claim: The canon constraint r_T(V) <= 1 of the optimum can be dropped: max-endurance/max-range are then returned at a speed the drive train cannot hold, instead of no_level_flight_speed or a declared full_throttle bound.
evidence: Production `return speed if speed.point.r_t <= 1.0 else _FULL_THROTTLE` replaced by `return speed`: 298 passed. No test in the file mentions `full_throttle` as a bound (only `full_throttle_thrust`, `propeller_table`, `stall_speed`, `level_flight_solution`, `mach_limit`).
recommended_test: Fast, test_endurance_and_range_optimum.py, two tests with endurance_builders. (1) SpeedOpti(a=0.06, b=0.0), stall-speed 19.0 m/s: D = 0.06 V^2 = 21.7 N at 19 m/s exceeds the full-throttle thrust at every speed from there on, expect FormulaError code no_level_flight_speed (verified on unmutated code; the mutant returns t_max = 280.8 s). (2) SpeedOpti(a=0.0, b=9000.0), stall-speed 6.0: expect an optimum_at_domain_bound warning with detail.bound == 'full_throttle' (edge about 43.3 m/s) and no postcondition_violated warning (verified; the mutant reports propeller_table and a violated postcondition).

original_probe.mutation: `return speed if speed.point.r_t <= 1.0 else _FULL_THROTTLE` -> `return speed` (r_T <= 1 constraint dropped)
original_probe.note: Not equivalent: with SpeedOpti(a=0.06, b=0), v_s = 19 the mutant returns 280.8 s where the original raises no_level_flight_speed.

claim: The axis origin of a partial-extent spar (root rib of ITS segment; offset in normal mode, absolute in standard mode) is unproven: a spar in an outboard segment could be placed from y = 0 and reported present/absent at the wrong stations. (Module is unreachable until gh-1429, so no user value is wrong today.)
evidence: `wing_ = two_rib_wing(fields, tip=(0.0, 0.5, 0.0), tip_chord=0.2)` - every fixture with spare_start/spare_length has its segment root at xyz_le y = 0.0, so `root.xyz_le[1] + offset` equals `offset`. Mutation `return root.xyz_le[1] + offset, slope` -> `return offset, slope`: all spar tests pass. test_standard_mode_origin_is_an_absolute_point (line 538) uses the same root, so the two tests assert identical numbers (0.24 absent, 0.26 present) for the two rules.
recommended_test: Fast, test_spar_capacity.py. (1) wing([spar(section=RECTANGULAR, material='test')], [spar(section=RECTANGULAR, material='test', spare_start=0.1, spare_length=0.2)]) (ribs at y = 0, 0.5, 1.0): y 0.55 -> NoSparAtStation, 0.6, 0.65, 0.8 -> BendingCapacity, 0.85 -> NoSparAtStation (verified on unmutated code). (2) Same two-segment wing, second-segment spar with spare_vector [0,1,0], spare_origin [0,0.2,0], spare_start 0.05: mode 'normal' present from y = 0.5+0.2+0.05 = 0.75; mode 'standard' present from y = 0.2+0.05 = 0.25, i.e. over the whole segment from 0.5.

original_probe.mutation: `return root.xyz_le[1] + offset, slope` -> `return offset, slope` (origin not relative to the segment root)
original_probe.note: Not equivalent: a partial spar in a segment starting at y = 0.5 moves by 0.5 m.

Reproduction (not a mutation): endurance_and_range_optimum(bound(SLUG, {'stall-speed': 0.0}), context_of(SLUG, SpeedOpti(min_speed=1.0))) did not return and was killed by SIGALRM after 15 s. No test passes a stall speed <= 0 to this formula.

claim: The declared limit of a sustained turn (thrust vs wing, ADR 0020 notice) can be the verdict at n_lim instead of the one the bisection met: a thrust-limited turn would be declared wing-limited.
evidence: `assert got.limit == expected[1]` at 20 m/s, n_lim 6, where the wing stops both at n_lim and at the answer; the formula tests accept either: `assert declared in (['thrust'], ['wing'])`. Mutation `high, stop = middle, found` -> `high = middle`: 298 passed.
recommended_test: Fast, test_powered_flight.py: got = await pf.sustained_load_factor(flight(), 28.0, 10.0); expect got.limit == 'thrust' and got.n == pb.sustained_n(28.0, 3.4, 10.0)[0] = 4.34764 (rel 1e-5). At n = 10 the wing stops the turn (C_L = 10*33.34/240.1 = 1.39 > 1.2) while the thrust binds first at n = 4.35, so the two labels differ (verified on unmutated code).

original_probe.mutation: `high, stop = middle, found` -> `high = middle` (limit label from the verdict at n_lim)

claim: The golden-section refinement may evaluate speeds below the scan start when the best scan point is the start itself; on airframes whose sweep has no lift peak there (gh-1419) the formula would end as not_converged again.
evidence: `low = max(speeds[best] - step, start)` -> `low = speeds[best] - step`: 298 passed. test_a_sweep_without_a_peak_below_the_scan_start_does_not_end_the_formula asserts `min(v for v, _ in opti.evaluations) >= start - 1e-9`, but none of its six optima sits on the first scan point.
recommended_test: Fast, test_powered_flight.py: record the arguments of f(v) = -v, call pf.maximise_over_speed(f, flight(), 9.5); expect min(recorded) >= 9.5 and 9.5 <= optimum.v < 9.51 (unmutated code gives 9.50005 and a minimum of 9.5).

original_probe.note: Not equivalent: with the best scan point at the start the search evaluates down to start - 2 m/s.

evidence: `for low, high in reversed(covered_pairs(points)):` -> without reversed(): 298 passed. Every table fixture (APC 13x8E, small_table flat C_P) has a single sign change.

evidence: `opti = pb.PolarOpti()  # 3.4 kg: T_0 = 60 N > W = 33.3 N, no lower stall bound from the angle`; module docstring: 'a static thrust of 60 N'. claim: The turn kinematics have no hand-computed value: the test re-types the production expression, so a wrong relation typed twice would pass (kernel rule: every formula against a hand-computed value).
evidence: Test helper: `return pb.G * math.sqrt(n * n - 1.0) / v` and `return -(v * v / (pb.G * math.sqrt(n * n - 1.0)))`; production: `return g * math.sqrt(n * n - 1.0) / v`.
